records.quote: the striking of the keys typed out your letters and, by their frequency and pauses, simultaneously tapped out telegraphic code, an outside operator could read your letters at the same moment they were being written.
records.paraphrase: Explanation that keystroke timing simultaneously produced typed text and readable Morse code.

records.quote: At one o'clock," the scientist went on, "you must issue orders for a gigantic deal of some sort; and you must issue them precisely as you have issued them in the past; there must be no variation. Dictate the letters as you have always done to Miss Winthrop--_but don't send them_!
records.paraphrase: He designs a controlled test using a fake deal to reproduce and confirm the leak.

records.quote: Grayson sat staring at him incredulously. "I still don't understand," he said finally.
records.paraphrase: The financier reacts with disbelief and confusion at the explanation.

records.quote: In the sciences we must be exact--not approximately so, but absolutely so. We must know. It isn't like carpentry. A carpenter may make a trivial mistake in a joint, and it will not weaken his house; but if the scientist makes one mistake, the whole structure tumbles down.
records.paraphrase: The scientist articulates a method emphasizing exactness, observation, and logic.

records.quote: If it is honest--merely business--to juggle stocks as you told me you did, this is no more dishonest.
records.paraphrase: The scientist contrasts the stenographer's scheme with the financier's own stock manipulation as morally equivalent.

records.quote: in writing on the typewriter, she was clever enough to be able to _give the click of the machine the patterns in the Morse telegraphic code_--so that another telegraph operator at the other end of the 'phone could hear her machine and translate the clicks into words.
records.paraphrase: The detective explains that the stenographer encoded typewriter key-clicks as Morse code that a listening operator could translate.

records.quote: The Thinking Machine sat beside him, squinting across the room in deep abstraction, and listening intently. His head was turned away from the reporter, but his ear was within a few inches of the machine.
records.paraphrase: He tests typewriters by listening carefully to the sound each machine makes.

records.quote: It happens that the little silver box which you gave Miss Winthrop is just tall enough to lift this receiver clear of the hook, and the minute the receiver is off the hook the line is open.
records.paraphrase: He describes how a silver box propped the phone receiver up to keep the line open so sound could travel out.

criteria.rationale: The story invokes the ideal of scientific exactness and applies real acoustic/telegraphic principles (Morse code encoding via keystroke rhythms), but this is applied deduction rather than a materially represented scientific fact or discovery; the reading is plausible but uncertain in materiality.

The engineered technique—encoding typewriter keystrokes as Morse code over an open telephone line propped by a silver box—is the crux of the plot, causing the leak that costs millions. This device/technique materially drives the setting, problem, and outcome.
The story is set in a contemporary period with no speculative future, remote past, or temporal displacement.

The clever exploitation combining stenography and telegraphy is worked out from real technical premises of the era's telephone and Morse systems, but the story largely presents an existing scheme rather than developing extended consequences from a premise; materiality of extrapolation is uncertain.

The detective systematically observes (listening to typewriter sounds), forms hypotheses, eliminates impossibilities by logic, and designs a controlled test using a fake deal to reproduce and confirm the leak—observation, hypothesis, and testing materially drive the resolution.
No other planets, dimensions, nonordinary cosmic environments, or visitors from them appear; the setting is an ordinary city office.
The financial losses are a personal/business misfortune to one man, not a large-scale natural, technological, cosmic, biological, or human-caused disaster.

candidates.description: A stenographer-typist who is also a telegraph operator encodes dictated letters into Morse code through the frequency and pauses of her typewriter keystrokes, which travel over a covertly opened telephone line (held open by a silver box propping the receiver) to a listening operator who transcribes them in real time -- constituting the 'leak' of the financier's secret plans.

novelty.rationale: The scheme relies entirely on ordinary, existing technology of the story's empirical norm: a standard typewriter, a standard extension telephone, Morse code, and a trained human operator's dexterity. Nothing in the storyworld is altered or made totalizingly different from the authorial empirical reality; the detective himself calls it 'nothing very mysterious... merely clever.' It is an ingenious application of known means, not a world-altering difference, so novelty is absent.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The method is given a coherent, systematic, nonsupernatural account: keystrokes produce both text and Morse rhythm; the silver box holds the receiver off the hook to keep the line open; the sound travels to a listening operator. The detective validates it through a controlled reproduction test (dictating a fake deal without sending it) and by listening to typewriters, reflecting an explicit method of observation and logic. The mechanism is internally consistent and immanent.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The concealed keystroke-Morse leak is the central mystery that governs the entire narrative: the financier's problem, the detective's investigation, the experiments, and the resolution all revolve around discovering and explaining this mechanism. It is not incidental but determines the whole narrative logic.

estrangement.rationale: The reader encounters the surprising contrast that ordinary typing sounds can secretly double as telegraphy, and the story frames the resulting espionage as morally equivalent to the financier's own stock manipulation. Grayson's incredulity marks the defamiliarizing effect, but this estrangement is recorded separately from the dimension assessments.
